Burst lines and backed-up drains do not wait for office hours. An AI voice agent answers, finds out whether water is still moving, and gets the call to the right plumber.

Plumbing calls come in at the worst possible times

An AI receptionist for plumbers picks up when you are under a house, on another job or asleep, and gets each caller to the right next step: a booked visit, a message, or a live transfer to whoever is on call tonight.

Irregular hours are built into the trade. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics notes that plumbers often work nights and weekends and are often on call to handle emergencies. That means the phone rings when the office is closed, and the person who answers is often the same plumber who just finished a twelve-hour day.

Plumbing callers are also usually stressed. Someone standing in an inch of water by the dishwasher wants to hear a calm voice ask sensible questions, not a voicemail greeting. We set up an AI voice agent on HighLevel that does exactly that: it asks your questions in your order, writes down the answers, and follows your rules about who gets woken up.

A night call, step by step

Here is the shape of a typical after-hours call once your rules are loaded. It is a generic example, not a recording, and every line in it is something you would sign off on first.

  1. The agent answers with your company name. It says it is the after-hours line and asks how it can help.
  2. Is water moving right now? This is the question that splits the night. Water still running from a pipe, a water heater or a supply line is handled differently from a slow drain that can wait until morning.
  3. Can they reach the shutoff? If you approved it, the agent asks whether the caller knows where the main shutoff is and reminds them to close it. If you did not, it skips this step.
  4. Where is the problem? Kitchen, bathroom, water heater, outside line, sewer backup. The answer goes in the notes so the plumber knows what to load.
  5. Address, access and callback number. Gate codes, pets, whether the caller is the owner or a tenant, and the best number to reach them.
  6. Route it. If the call meets your emergency rules, the agent transfers it to your on-call number. If not, it books the first morning opening or takes a message, and tells the caller what to expect in the words you chose.

Nothing in that flow requires the agent to know plumbing. It requires your judgment, written down once, which the agent then applies to every caller the same way.

What the agent says, and what it is not allowed to say

Lines you can approve

  • Your service area, hours and after-hours policy, including any after-hours fee you want stated
  • Whether you work on tankless water heaters, well systems, sewer lines or commercial buildings
  • A reminder to close the main shutoff, if that is your preference
  • What happens next and roughly when to expect a callback, in your words, without a promised arrival time
  • A flat service-call or drain price, but only if you publish one

Lines it will not say

  • Walk a caller through a repair or tell them a fixture is safe to use
  • Diagnose the cause of a leak, a clog or a water heater fault
  • Price a replacement or a repair it has not seen
  • Dispatch a plumber or promise an arrival time
  • Troubleshoot a gas smell (it tells the caller to leave and call 911 or the gas utility from outside)

The gas rule matters for plumbers who install or repair gas water heaters and lines. Federal pipeline safety guidance from PHMSA tells people who suspect a gas leak to leave the area and call 911 from a neighbor's house or another location well away from the leak, and to avoid using phones or switches near it. So the agent does not ask follow-up questions about the smell. It reads the safety line, ends the call, and alerts you.

On-call routing without a phone tree

Small plumbing companies usually handle nights one of three ways: the owner carries the phone, the plumbers rotate, or calls go to voicemail until morning. An AI agent works with the first two and replaces the third.

  • Live transfer for true emergenciesHighLevel's voice AI can transfer a call to a human phone number, so a caller with active water can be put straight through to the plumber on call.
  • A rotation you can changeWhen the on-call plumber changes each week, the transfer number changes with it. Updating it is part of our monthly service.
  • Written summaries for everything elseNon-urgent calls arrive by email with the caller's name, address, problem and callback number, ready for the morning schedule.
  • A record of every callCalls and messages are logged in a HighLevel pipeline, so the office can see what came in overnight before the first truck leaves.

The calls that are not emergencies, and why they still count

Most plumbing calls are not floods. They are a water heater that takes forever to recover, a toilet that runs all night, a slow shower drain, a faucet that drips, a homeowner who wants a sewer camera inspection before buying a house. These are the calls that fill the schedule on a normal Tuesday, and they are easy to lose when nobody answers.

Small leaks add up. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's WaterSense program says household leaks can waste nearly 1 trillion gallons of water annually nationwide. A homeowner who finally calls about a running toilet or a dripping supply line is ready to book, and the agent can put them on your calendar on the first ring.

For these calls the agent books straight into the time slots you set aside, collects the details you need (water heater fuel type and age, which drain, whether it is a rental), and sends you the summary.

An AI receptionist for home services, and the follow-up after the call

Plumbing is one of many home service businesses with the same problem: the owner is also the best technician, and the phone pulls them off the job. An AI receptionist for home services is only the front end. Home service business automation is what happens after the call, and it is where a lot of jobs are won or lost.

  • Each caller becomes a contact in a HighLevel CRM pipeline, with stages you choose, such as new call, booked, estimate sent, job done
  • Estimates for repiping or water heater replacement get an automated email follow-up if the homeowner has not answered
  • Finished jobs can trigger a review request by email
  • With AI Pro, an outbound voice agent can call back customers who asked to be reminded about a water heater flush or a drain maintenance visit

Texting is not live yet. Voice works today. Text messages (missed call text back, text reminders and texted review requests) switch on once carrier approval clears; that approval is the A2P 10DLC registration US carriers require for business texting from a regular local number. Until then, confirmations, follow-ups and review requests go out by email.

Your software, your prices, your call

If your company already uses field service software to run the schedule, the agent does not replace it. Whether booked calls can flow into that software depends on the software and your account, so we check and confirm it per client before we promise it. When a direct connection is not available, bookings go into a HighLevel calendar and your office enters them as usual.

AI Starter, at $597 a month, adds CRM automation setup, review management, monthly reporting and email support, and AI Pro, at $1,097 a month, adds outbound calling and full CRM automation. Setup, training and support are included in every package. Details are on the pricing page, and the AI answering service page explains how this compares with a traditional answering service.

Questions plumbers ask before putting AI on the phone

Can an AI receptionist for plumbers handle emergency calls at night?

It can answer them, sort them and pass them on. You tell us what an emergency means for your company, for example water actively running, no water to the house, or sewage coming up a drain. When a night caller matches, the agent transfers the call to your on-call plumber or marks the message urgent. Everything else becomes a message or a booked morning slot. It does not send anyone to the job; your on-call plumber decides that.

What does the AI tell a caller with a burst pipe?

Only what you approved. Many plumbers want callers asked whether they know where their main shutoff is and, if they do, reminded to close it. Some prefer the agent say nothing about valves at all. Either way, the wording is yours, written once and read the same way every time. The agent does not walk callers through repairs, and if a caller mentions a gas smell it tells them to leave the home and call 911 or the gas utility from outside.

Will the AI quote prices for a water heater or drain cleaning?

Only the prices you choose to publish. Some plumbing companies want the agent to state a flat service-call fee or a drain cleaning price; others want every price question answered with "the plumber will give you a price after looking at it." The agent will never guess at a replacement cost or price a job it has not seen.

Is there an AI receptionist for home services besides plumbing?

Yes. The same setup works for most home service businesses that take calls from homeowners: HVAC, electrical, roofing, remodeling, pest control, cleaning. The questions and the urgent rules change by trade. See our pages for HVAC companies and contractors, or the general AI receptionist page.

Can it text the customer when the plumber is on the way?

Not yet. Voice works today, and confirmations can go out by email now. Text messages switch on once our carrier registration (A2P 10DLC) is approved. Until then we do not promise any text feature.
